SATOM Builder

SATOM Builder is a separate tool, installed on its own server next to SATOM, where authors build views, widgets and Plugin Studio apps (optionally with AI) and check them with SATOM's own rules; SATOM gives it per-author API tokens, the /api/v1/builder endpoints, the rules pack and trusted publishers.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio studio.script_library users.manage
📍 WhereSATOM side — Administrator → API Tokens (one token per author), Report Studio or Plugin Studio → Apps → Trusted publishers (URL /plugins/publishers), and the API at https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1/builder/*

What is it?#

SATOM Builder is a separate tool that customers install on another server, next to SATOM — never on the SATOM node itself. Authors use it to build Report Studio views and widgets and Plugin Studio apps, optionally drafting them with an AI model, and to check every package with SATOM's own rules before it reaches SATOM. It talks to SATOM only through the API, with each author's own token.

This article describes what SATOM provides for the Builder. How to install and use the Builder itself is in the Builder's own documentation.

What does it do?#

On the SATOM side:

  • One API token per author. Every Builder call runs with the token of the person working, so it carries that person's permissions and ADOM, and the audit log names them. SATOM stays the authority.
  • The /api/v1/builder/* endpoints (table below): describe this server, hand out the rules pack, validate, rehearse and import a package, and register a publisher key.
  • The rules pack — SATOM's own package check as a zip the Builder runs locally (see The rules pack). SATOM checks every package again on validate, rehearse and import.
  • The test runtime (SATOM 4.2.0 and later) — the same zip also carries the view renderer and frame, the diagram walk, the data-store rules, the script jail and the script SDK, copied byte for byte. The Builder tests a package with them on its own test data (generated rows with this server's dataset columns, canned connection answers, chosen answers for device steps), on the Builder, with no network: nothing of a test run reaches SATOM.
  • The library (SATOM 4.2.0 and later) — /builder/library shows authors what they build on: the datasets and their columns, the data stores and their column definitions, the API Catalog with every version's endpoints, and the API library of the token's ADOM (builds, a build's endpoints, an endpoint's fields). Structure only: never a row of data, never a secret.
  • This server's data for the test data (SATOM 4.3.0 and later) — /builder/data lets an author start testing on what this server holds instead of generated rows: the rows a view rendered here would show the token's owner (their ADOM's devices, no maintenance device without the permission, the audit log only with the audit permission, sensitive columns masked), the data stores' rows (declared columns and _id) and the lists of satom_select fields, at most 2,000 rows per table. The rows stay on the author's Builder, where its Database tab shows them as tables with a diagram and a read-only SQL console; they never travel in a package and never reach the Builder's AI. Each read leaves an audit line builder.data.
  • Every dataset, in line with this server (SATOM 4.3.0 and later) — the Builder lists, tests and packages with the same datasets this server offers its plugins: the built-in ones, one per device-object type its cache holds and the ones its administrators publish. A view's package carries the definition of the administrator datasets it reads; a server without one creates it pending its administrator's approval. See the Plugin Studio section for the whole path.
  • Apps on a schedule (SATOM 4.5.0 and later) — an app package may carry "automations": the app run by Automations (action "Run a Plugin Studio app") every N minutes, daily, weekly, monthly or on a cron line, with the form values it runs with. The Builder's editor has an Automations tab for them; the import creates each one switched off, run as the importing user once an administrator publishes the app and switches it on. A diagram reads the devices SATOM manages with the Read SATOM's appliances step (satom_appliances).
  • Fortinet APIs without invented paths (SATOM 4.5.0 and later) — a connection pinned to a build of SATOM's API library ("api": "fortigate", "api_version": "8.0.1") carries that build as an API Catalog version: every REST endpoint the build serves, from /builder/library/fortinet/<product>/<version>/catalog. The Builder adds it to the package, puts the build's endpoint list in front of its AI, and the check refuses an api_call whose path is not one of them — in the Builder and again here. Before calling a generated app done, the Builder runs it on test data with SATOM's own runtime (answers in the device's own shape); an app on a schedule that writes without reading first is run a second time with every entry already on the device, so a daily run that would fail tomorrow is caught today.
  • Trusted publishers — the Builder signs its packages with its own Ed25519 publisher key; registered in SATOM, its packages read as signed (see Manage trusted publishers).
  • The builder policy — everything that arrives from the Builder is checked with the stricter builder rules (see What the importer checks).
  • Secrets stay in SATOM. A package never carries a password or token. The secret of each connection an import creates is typed by the author, relayed once with the import call and stored by SATOM only (the vault, or encrypted in the database); it is never written to the audit log.

The endpoints#

All paths are under https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1. Package bodies are multipart/form-data: package (the .satomplugin file, at most 10 MB) and an optional options field holding a JSON object.

Method Path Scope The token's owner also needs What it does
GET /builder/target read — Describes this server for the rules: SATOM version, the rules pack's SHA-256, the token's ADOM, who is calling (scopes, may author, may import), the choices the app editor offers, the plugin datasets, the Examples templates, the apps, data stores, connections (only whether each has a secret, never the secret), API versions and scripts that exist, the enabled publishers of the ADOM and the schema
GET /builder/rules-pack read — The rules pack zip, satom-rules-<version>-<sha12>.zip, with the header X-Satom-Rules-Sha256; from 4.2.0 it also carries the test runtime (runtime in rules.json)
GET /builder/library read — What a plugin builds on: every dataset of the token's ADOM — built-in, administrator (admin_…, with its query) and one per cached device-object type (4.3.0) — with its columns, relations and masked fields; data stores with their columns, the API Catalog with every version's endpoints, the API library builds of the token's ADOM (4.2.0)
GET /builder/library/fortinet/<product>/<version> read — One API library build's endpoints; with ?endpoint=<name> that endpoint's fields and how they were measured. A product outside the token's ADOM is 403 wrong_product (4.2.0)
GET /builder/library/fortinet/<product>/<version>/catalog read — That build as an API Catalog version, exactly as an app package carries it in "apis" ("source": "library"): FortiGate tables with {key} paths and their lists as child endpoints, FortiWeb/FortiADC with ?mkey=, FortiAuthenticator <resource>/{id}/. 404 not_measured, 422 no_paths (FortiAnalyzer) (4.5.0)
GET /builder/data read studio.script_library (a Plugin Studio author) This server's rows for the Builder's test data: datasets, stores (comma lists; empty = none; absent = every store, and the built-in and administrator datasets — a device-object dataset only when named) and limit (rows per table, 1 to 2,000, default 200). Datasets as a view rendered here shows the owner, data stores with their declared columns and _id, the satom_select lists; at most 3 MB, a cut table says truncated (4.3.0)
POST /builder/validate write — Checks the package with the builder rules against this server; writes nothing. HTTP 200 even when ok is false: ok, problems, warnings, summary (kind, slug, version, signer, what it creates and keeps, which connections need a secret, where it lands)
POST /builder/rehearse write studio.script_library (a Plugin Studio author) Checks the package, then walks an app's diagram unarmed against this server's data stores, connections and secrets, or renders a view or widget in the plugin sandbox. Installs nothing
POST /builder/import admin studio.plugin_studio (a super-admin) The console's import, with the same checks and install; options: allow_downgrade, secrets
GET /builder/publishers read — The registered publisher keys: key_id, label, enabled, created_at
POST /builder/publishers admin studio.plugin_studio Registers a publisher key: {"label": …, "public_key": "<base64 of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key>"}

The POST endpoints are limited to 30 calls per minute. See SATOM API for the answers and error codes.

Requirements#

  • A SATOM release that offers /api/v1/builder/*.
  • SATOM Builder installed on its own server, able to reach SATOM over HTTPS.
  • The ADOM each author works in must have the API Tokens capability (see API tokens).

Permissions#

A token never does more than its owner. Each call needs the token's scope, the permission that scope maps to on the owner, and for some calls a Studio permission on top:

Builder action Token scope The owner must hold
Read the target, download the rules pack, list publishers read view (any view permission)
Validate on SATOM write config_write
Load from SATOM (test data) read view and studio.script_library
Rehearse on SATOM write config_write and studio.script_library
Import into SATOM admin users.manage and studio.plugin_studio
Register the publisher key admin users.manage and studio.plugin_studio

studio.plugin_studio is seeded on the Administrator profile only. Creating the tokens needs users.manage; managing trusted publishers in the console needs studio.plugin_studio.

How to use#

  1. 1TokensAn administrator creates one token per author in SATOM
  2. 2PublisherA super-admin registers the Builder's publisher key
  3. 3BuildThe author builds and checks the package in the Builder
  4. 4Validate / rehearseSATOM checks it again and walks it unarmed
  5. 5ImportSATOM installs it with the secrets the author types

Create a token for each author#

  1. In SATOM, open Administrator → API Tokens (see API tokens).
  2. Create a token with the author as Owner (inherits RBAC), bound to the ADOM the author builds for.
  3. Tick the scopes the author needs: read to validate locally, write to validate and rehearse on SATOM, admin to import and to register the publisher key. A scope the owner's permissions do not cover is refused.
  4. Copy the token (it is shown once) and give it to the author, who pastes it in the Builder under My tokens.

Use one token per person, never a shared one: the import, its audit line and the ADOM it lands in follow the token's owner.

Register the Builder's publisher key#

Either way works, and registering the same key twice changes nothing:

  • From the Builder: the author opens Publisher key → Register on target. This calls POST /builder/publishers with the author's token, which needs the admin scope and a super-admin owner. A key registered this way is trusted in every ADOM.
  • In SATOM by hand: a super-admin copies the public key from the Builder's Publisher key page and adds it under Trusted publishers (see Manage trusted publishers), optionally limited to some ADOMs.

A view or widget signed by a registered publisher lands in testing; without the key registered, a signed package is refused.

Validate, rehearse and import#

  1. Validate (write): SATOM checks the package with the builder rules against this server and writes nothing. Fix every problem it lists.
  2. Rehearse (write, a Plugin Studio author): for an app, give the form inputs and choose how Ask a person steps are answered (yes, no or stop). Write steps and script steps are recorded as rehearsal: not executed; reads run for real against this server's data stores and connections. Nothing is installed and no run record is kept. A view or widget comes back rendered with this server's datasets, cut to the token's owner.
  3. Import (admin, a super-admin): send the package with the secrets of the connections it creates ("secrets": {"<connection id>": "<secret>"}). SATOM installs it exactly like the console's import: an app lands as a draft, a view or widget in testing (publisher-signed) or draft (unsigned), in the token's ADOM.
  4. In SATOM, review the imported object, test it and Publish it, as for any imported package.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -F package=@ip-owner-1.0.0.satomplugin \
  https://satom.example.com/api/v1/builder/validate
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -F package=@ip-owner-1.0.0.satomplugin \
  -F 'options={"secrets": {"ddi": "s3cret"}}' \
  https://satom.example.com/api/v1/builder/import

Configuration#

options of the package endpoints:

Endpoint Field Description Example
rehearse inputs The form values of the app, an object {"host": "app-01"}
rehearse answers How Ask a person is answered: yes (default), no, or stop (the walk stops and returns waiting with the prompt) "stop"
import allow_downgrade Install an older version over a newer one false
import secrets {connection id: secret} for the connections the import creates. A value for a connection that already exists is ignored and reported in kept; an empty value or one longer than 8 KiB is dropped {"ddi": "…"}

Result#

  • validate and rehearse write nothing but their audit line.
  • import answers ok, kind, slug, version, lands_in, created, kept, todo, problems, warnings, signed_by, signer and policy. created lists secret of connection … for each secret stored. problems are the installed app's own problems (for example a connection whose secret was not given).
  • The audit log records builder.target, builder.rules_pack, builder.validate, builder.rehearse and builder.import.refused with the token and its owner; a successful import writes the same entry as the console (studio.app.import, plugin.import or plugin.code.install) with the token attached, and a registration writes plugin.publisher.add. A secret is never in any of them.

Troubleshooting#

403 insufficient_scope — "This endpoint requires the '…' scope."#

Possible causes - The token lacks the scope the call needs: write for validate and rehearse, admin for import and publisher registration.

Solution 1. In SATOM, Edit the token under Administrator → API Tokens and tick the scope (the owner must hold the permission it maps to).

Verification - GET /api/v1/ping lists the scope.

403 owner_forbidden#

Possible causes - The token owner lacks the permission this scope maps to ('…'). — the owner lost config_write (write) or user_manage (admin). - The token's owner is not a Plugin Studio author (studio.script_library). — on rehearse, and on reading this server's data for the test data. - Importing needs a super-admin owner (studio.plugin_studio). — on import. - Registering a publisher needs a super-admin owner (studio.plugin_studio).

Solution 1. Give the owner the permission in Users and profiles, or let a super-admin do the import or registration with their own token.

403 wrong_product — "The token's owner may not work in the ADOM this token is bound to."#

Possible causes - The owner's ADOM access no longer includes the token's ADOM.

Solution 1. Restore the owner's access to that ADOM, or create a token bound to an ADOM the owner may enter.

"The package is signed by a key this server does not trust (…)."#

Possible causes - The Builder's publisher key is not registered in SATOM, is disabled, or is limited to other ADOMs than the token's. Validate reports it as a package.format problem; import answers 422.

Solution 1. Register or enable the key — see Register the Builder's publisher key.

Verification - GET /builder/target lists the publisher under publishers.

422 package_refused#

Possible causes - The import found problems: the message says the package breaks N rule(s) of the builder policy (or names the one rule the importer enforces itself, such as a code plugin or min_satom), and problems lists each one with where and message.

Solution 1. Fix every problem in the Builder, validate again (it uses the same check), then import.

Rehearse: "… is not on this server yet: import the package first"#

Possible causes - The app uses a data store, connection or script that the package would create and that does not exist on this server yet. A rehearsal never invents an object; it answers status: "failed" with the package needs objects this server does not have yet.

Solution 1. Import the package first (it lands as a draft), then rehearse; or rehearse on a server that already has those objects.

"… needs SATOM … or newer (this server runs …)"#

Possible causes - The package's min_satom is newer than this server. The Builder sets it to the version of the SATOM the package was built for.

Solution 1. Update SATOM, or build the package for this server's version.

409 busy#

Possible causes - Too many rehearsals run at once on this server (two per web worker).

Solution 1. Retry after a moment.

413 too_large — "The package is larger than 10 MB."#

Solution 1. Make the package smaller: fewer or smaller images and seed rows.

400 invalid_key#

Possible causes - The publisher key sent to POST /builder/publishers is not the base64 of a raw 32-byte Ed25519 key, or the label is empty or longer than 80 characters. The message says which.

Advanced#

Advanced How SATOM stays the authority
  • GET /builder/target is exactly the target the rules pack's check takes, and the import page uses the same description of the server, so a package is judged against one description of SATOM whichever way it comes in.
  • The rules pack carries SATOM's own rule modules byte for byte; a module that needs the server (the database, Flask) is replaced by a stub that raises if it is used. It needs only jinja2, markupsafe and cryptography.
  • During a Builder call, SATOM acts as the token's owner: the ADOM an import is stamped with, the datasets a rehearsal may show and the audit line all follow that person.
Advanced Rehearsal limits

A rehearsal runs inside the web request: at most 60 seconds, two at a time per web worker, and at most 20 Ask a person answers before it stops. Password values typed as inputs are masked in the steps and outputs it returns.

#satom builder#builder#test data#mock data#builder data#test database#sql console#test run#library#plugin builder#app builder#package#satomplugin#validate#rehearse#import#rules pack#publisher key#trusted publisher#ai#api token#builder api
